_comment: MACHINE-READABLE SOURCE OF TRUTH for the /rentals/rights §02 'when a landlord asks for X' cards (and the §03 help + §04 sources lists). Structured twin of the coaching in landlord-tactics.md and the jurisdiction law/ topic files. When a card's verdict, response line, or citation changes, change it HERE — the Plain Sight rights page picks it up at build time via scripts/sync-law-data.mjs. Not legal advice; the page's as-of date comes from jurisdiction-facts.json (asOf). Each card: ask, verdict ('no' = not allowed/unsafe, 'ask' = conditional/know-the-limit), label (short chip), say (a calm sourced line to send), src, href (or null). Shared cards live in 'shared' and are referenced from a jurisdiction's list as {"ref":"<key>"} so a single edit propagates to every jurisdiction that uses it.

ssn.ask: Text or email your Social Security number to “hold” the unit
ssn.label: Don’t send it
ssn.say: I’m glad to complete screening through your application service, which handles that securely. I don’t send a Social Security number in a message thread.

overcollect.ask: Provide your last 3 tax returns and 3 months of bank statements
overcollect.label: More than needed
overcollect.say: I can provide standard proof of income — a recent redacted paystub or an employer letter. Is that sufficient for your screening?

inspections.ask: We inspect the unit on a routine schedule (e.g. every 45 days)
inspections.label: Not as a routine
inspections.say: Entry needs reasonable notice and a real reason; routine sweeps run against my right to quiet enjoyment. Can we put the entry policy in the lease?

selfhelp.ask: The lease ends immediately if the landlord decides something’s wrong (self-help)
selfhelp.label: Unenforceable
selfhelp.say: The law requires the legal eviction process. A clause allowing immediate self-help termination isn’t enforceable — I’d like it removed.

DC.ask: Pay first month + last month + a separate security deposit, all up front
DC.label: Over the DC cap
DC.say: In DC the security deposit is capped at one month’s rent, and money held as “last month’s rent” still counts toward that cap. Could you send the full up-front total, itemized, in writing?
DC.src: DC Office of the Tenant Advocate

DC.ask: The application fee is non-refundable even if you’re never screened
DC.label: Must be refunded
DC.say: DC requires an unused or never-run application fee to be refunded within 14 days. Could you confirm that in writing?

DC.ask: No pets — and breed or size restrictions on any animal
DC.label: Takes effect Oct 1, 2026
DC.say: DC’s Pets in Housing law (Roscoe’s Law) takes effect October 1, 2026 and will bar breed and size restrictions; and assistance animals already aren’t counted as “pets.” Could you confirm your policy against the current rules?

DC.ask: We don’t accept vouchers — and you must earn 3× the full rent
DC.label: Source-of-income discrimination
DC.say: In DC, refusing a voucher or subsidy is source-of-income discrimination, and an income test generally applies to my share of the rent, not the full rent.
DC.src: DC Office of Human Rights — fair housing

DC.ask: Your application was auto-rejected for an eviction filing or an old record
DC.label: Ask for a human
DC.say: Could I get individualized consideration by a person? An eviction filing without a judgment, or a sealed or dismissed case, isn’t a lawful basis for denial in DC.

MD.ask: Pay first month + last month + a separate security deposit, all up front
MD.label: Over the MD cap
MD.say: In Maryland the security deposit is capped at one month’s rent (leases on/after Oct 1, 2024), and last month’s rent paid in advance counts as a deposit. Could you itemize the full up-front total in writing?

MD.ask: A non-refundable screening fee, no cap
MD.label: MD fee limits
MD.say: For a landlord with five or more units, Maryland caps the screening fee at $25, and it must be waived if I provide a recent screening report. Could you confirm the fee?

MD.ask: We don’t accept vouchers — and you must earn 3× the full rent
MD.label: Source-of-income discrimination
MD.say: Maryland’s HOME Act bars refusing my voucher or subsidy, and a 2025 ruling (Hare v. David S. Brown) limits rigid income-ratio screens. The income test should apply to my share of the rent.

MD.ask: The rent goes up whatever amount we decide at renewal
MD.label: County rent caps
MD.say: In Montgomery and Prince George’s County, annual rent increases are capped. If this unit is in either county, could you point me to the current allowable increase?

MD.ask: Your application was auto-rejected for a record
MD.label: Ask for a human
MD.say: Montgomery County limits criminal- and credit-history screening, so a filing or an old record isn’t an automatic bar. Could I get individualized consideration?

VA.ask: First month + last month + up to two months’ deposit, all up front
VA.label: Legal in VA — negotiate
VA.say: In Virginia this stack is legal — first, last, and up to two months’ deposit — which is the main reason move-in costs here run high. I’d like to negotiate the deposit down or spread it over the first months.

VA.label: VA caps it at $50
VA.say: Virginia caps the application fee at $50. Could you confirm the fee before I apply?

VA.ask: Several months of rent prepaid up front
VA.label: Must go to escrow
VA.say: Virginia doesn’t cap prepaid rent, but it must be placed in escrow by the end of the fifth business day after the landlord receives it. Where will it be held?

VA.label: Source-of-income discrimination
VA.say: Virginia has prohibited source-of-income discrimination since 2020, so refusing my voucher or subsidy isn’t allowed.

VA.ask: Your application was auto-rejected for a dismissed eviction case
VA.label: Dismissed cases expunge
VA.say: Virginia automatically expunges dismissed eviction cases (HB 73), so a dismissed filing isn’t a lawful basis for denial. Could you reconsider with that in mind?
